metaTitle: India to Korea Visa: Do You Need One? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Yes — Indian passport holders need a visa for South Korea (C-3-9 short-term tourist, up to 90 days). Here's exactly where to apply, the documents and where to get each, fees and processing time.

verdict.headline: Yes — Indian passport holders need a visa.
verdict.sub: You'll apply for the C-3-9 short-term tourist visa (single entry, stay up to 90 days) in person at a Korea Visa Application Center. K-ETA/visa-free entry does NOT apply to Indian passports.
verdict.entry: Single entry (multiple-entry possible in some cases — ask at KVAC)

tldr: Fill the form at visa.go.kr (the ONLY official portal), print and sign it.
Walk in (no appointment) to the Korea Visa Application Center for YOUR state — India has two jurisdictions.
Bring passport, photo, flight + hotel reservations, 6-month bank statement, and 2–3 years of ITR.
Fee ≈ INR 3,400 + service fee; result in about 5–10 working days.

jurisdiction.title: Step 0 — Find YOUR center (this trips people up)
jurisdiction.intro: India is split into two consular jurisdictions. You must apply at the center that covers your state of residence — showing up at the wrong one wastes the trip. This is the single most common mistake.

zones.name: Embassy of Korea — New Delhi jurisdiction
zones.covers: Most of India: North, West, East & Central states (Delhi NCR, Maharashtra, Gujarat, West Bengal, UP, Punjab, etc.)

zones.name: Consulate General — Chennai jurisdiction
zones.covers: South India: Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana & Puducherry

jurisdiction.note: Not sure which is yours? Open the KVAC site for your region and check its jurisdiction/center list before travelling to submit.

items.title: Confirm the visa type
items.detail: For tourism you want the C-3-9 short-term visit (tourist) visa. Gather the checklist below before you start.

items.title: Fill the form at visa.go.kr
items.detail: Go to the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) — the only official site. Complete the application form online, then print and sign it. One form per applicant.

items.title: Assemble your documents
items.detail: Collect every document in the checklist below. Missing financials or a wrong-format photo are the top reasons for delays.

items.title: Go to your KVAC — no appointment
items.detail: Walk in to the Korea Visa Application Center for your jurisdiction during working hours. No appointment is required in India.

items.title: Submit & pay
items.detail: Hand over your form + documents and pay the visa fee plus the center service fee at the counter.

items.title: Track your application
items.detail: Follow the status by email/SMS or on the KVAC tracking page. Don't book non-refundable flights until you're approved.

items.title: Collect your passport
items.detail: Pick up in person or by courier. Check the visa sticker details (name, dates, entry type) the moment you receive it.

documents.title: Document checklist — with where & how to get each
documents.intro: This is the part every other site skips. For each document, here is exactly where you obtain it and what it must show.

rows.how: Valid 6+ months beyond your trip, at least 2 blank pages, issued within the last 10 years. Bring old passports too.
Complete on the Korea Visa Portal, print, and sign. One per applicant.
White background, taken within the last 6 months, full face, no glasses or headwear.
A confirmed reservation/itinerary is enough — do NOT buy a paid ticket before the visa is approved.
Confirmed hotel bookings covering your stay. Staying with someone? Add an invitation letter + host's ID/ARC copy.
Request a 6-month statement with the bank's seal/stamp and an authorized signature. A steady balance is far more convincing than a sudden deposit.
Download the ITR-V / acknowledgement for the last 2–3 years from the Income Tax e-filing portal.
Employed: leave letter + employment letter on company letterhead. Self-employed: business registration / GST. Student: bonafide certificate. Retired: pension proof.
A short letter stating trip purpose and dates, plus a day-by-day plan. Not always mandatory, but it strengthens a tourist file.
If you genuinely can't provide ITR or bank statements, include a signed letter explaining why.

funds.title: "How much bank balance do I need?"
funds.body: There is no single official minimum published for the tourist visa. What matters is proving you can comfortably fund the whole trip and have reasons to return to India. Case officers look at stability, not just a headline number.
tips: Show a consistent balance over 6 months — a large deposit made days before applying looks weak.
Pair the bank statement with your ITR; together they tell a credible story.
Being sponsored? Add the sponsor's bank statement, a signed sponsorship letter, and proof of your relationship.

items.d: Applying at a center that doesn't cover your state. Check your jurisdiction (Delhi vs Chennai) first.
A sudden large deposit right before applying. Show steady, explainable funds instead.
Paying for non-refundable tickets before approval. A reservation is enough for the file.
No income-tax returns and no explanation. If you can't file ITR, attach a clear explanation letter.
Wrong size, colored background, glasses or an old photo. Use a fresh 35×45 mm white-background shot.

items.q: Can Indians get a Korea visa on arrival or e-visa?
items.a: Not for standard tourism — Indian passport holders apply in advance for the C-3-9 tourist visa at a Korea Visa Application Center. The Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr) is where you fill the form; some categories support e-application there.
No. In India you can walk in to the KVAC during working hours and submit; no prior appointment is required.
Usually about 5–10 working days, but it can be longer during peak travel season or if extra checks are needed. Apply well ahead of your trip.
Roughly INR 3,400 for a single-entry short-term visa, plus the center's service fee (around INR 1,100–1,400). Amounts change — confirm the current fee at your KVAC.

items.q: Which center do I go to?
items.a: It depends on your state of residence. South Indian states go through the Chennai jurisdiction (Chennai, Bengaluru); the rest of India goes through the New Delhi/Embassy jurisdiction (New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and more).

items.q: Can I get a multiple-entry visa?
items.a: Multiple-entry tourist visas are possible in some cases (for example applicants with strong travel history), but eligibility varies. Ask at your KVAC or the consulate about current multiple-entry rules for India.

items.q: What if I've never filed ITR?
items.a: Submit a signed letter explaining why, and strengthen the file with a solid 6-month bank statement and, if relevant, a sponsor's documents.

items.q: Do I still need the e-Arrival Card after I get the visa?
items.a: The e-Arrival Card requirement can still apply on entry. Check the entry-document rules close to your travel date on the official sites.
